newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba to launch one-hour flash memory recorder.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to launch one-hour flash memory recorder.

text.p: A unit of Toshiba Corp said on Friday it would launch the industry's first flash memory voice recorder which can record up to one hour of sound.
Toshiba Video Products Japan Co Ltd said it would introduce two models of its Digital Memory Recorder Voicebar in Japan on July 16.
The pocket-sized devices are only one-third the weight of a microcasette recorder and sound can be recorded over, Toshiba Video Products said in a statement.

The DMR-60, which can record up to 60 minutes, has a 32-megabit integrated circuit (IC) memory, or flash memory, while the DMR-30, which can record up to 30 minutes, has a 16-megabit IC memory, it said.
The products will be priced at 19,500 yen and 14,000 yen respectively, and total annual sales are targetted at 30,000 units, it added.
Earlier versions of flash memory voice recorders by Toshiba and other electronics companies such as Sony Corp and Sanyo Electric Co Ltd had shorter recording times and were more expensive.
